tier_reason: The report's timing matrix matches the record (e.g. 16-bit CBR 192 kb/s encode 371.9126 vs 380.9057 ms, decode 95.3447 vs 99.9845 ms; 96.80-107.55x and 338.14-430.05x realtime). The harness is public (tools/raw_celt_bench.c, tools/run_raw_celt_bench.sh, tools/run_soundkit_flac_corpus.py), and the report names Rust 1.97.1, GCC 12.2.0, the Rust and C-driver flags and the Xeon Platinum 8581C. The corpus is private and only hashes of the raw timing JSONs are published, so these are first-party numbers with partial methodology: C, not A.

corrections.baseline: libopus, Opus trunk commit 03647f524a40b05a1898522e92033810b58103c7 (static .libs/libopus.a from an autotools tree; configure flags not recorded), called through the full opus_encode/opus_encode24 and opus_decode/opus_decode24 API
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Rust 1.97.1 / Cargo 1.97.1: release mode, ThinLTO, codegen-units=1, -C target-cpu=native. C driver tools/raw_celt_bench.c: GCC 12.2.0, -O3 -DNDEBUG -march=native, linked against the static libopus.a from the trunk commit. The libopus library's own configure string (optimisation level, intrinsics, --enable-float-approx) is recorded as unavailable. corrections.hardware: GCP c4-highcpu-4 (4 vCPUs), Intel Xeon Platinum 8581C; measured processes pinned to CPU 2 with taskset; one x86 host only
corrections.workload: 48 kHz stereo CELT-only, 5 ms (240-sample) frames, OPUS_APPLICATION_AUDIO, fullband, complexity 10, 16-bit and 24-bit PCM, CBR and constrained VBR at 192/256/320 kb/s. Direct in-process encode and decode of four 10 s excerpts from the private SoundKit diverse-v1 corpus. A 5 s warm-up, three alternating Rust/C rounds of seven internal repeats, the median per source, and four source medians summed per cell (40 s of audio). The C side runs the full Opus encoder/decoder layer (opus_encode with OPUS_SIGNAL_MUSIC). The Rust side runs the crate's own CELT-only raw-frame Encoder/Decoder.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 0 stars, 0 forks, 53 commits; archived 2026-08-25. crates.io libopus-rs 0.0.2 (2026-06-30, before the benchmarked August checkpoint), 4,277 downloads.
corrections.caveats: The gain is small (encode 1.19-2.36%, decode 1.50-4.64%) and covers one configuration family (48 kHz stereo CELT, 5 ms frames, maximum complexity, 192-320 kb/s) on one x86 host. The libopus.a build configuration was not recorded, and the project's own README warns that intrinsics and --enable-float-approx materially change the C baseline. Meanwhile the Rust side was built with target-cpu=native, ThinLTO and one codegen unit. At a 1-2% margin, build asymmetry cannot be ruled out. The work is not identical. C goes through the full opus_encode/opus_decode layer, including the 4 ms OPUS_APPLICATION_AUDIO delay compensation: the quality gate aligns C at 312 samples versus 120 for Rust. Rust is a CELT-only raw-frame codec that ports the tonality analysis but not that lookahead. Output is not bit-exact with libopus, and the README says the encoder does not target byte identity. CBR byte totals match (fixed by the bitrate), constrained-VBR totals differ by 350-527 B over 400 s, aligned SNR is within about 0.04 dB, and ViSQOL MOS-LQO is 4.5731 versus 4.5724. The packet-identity gate compares Rust with its own previous checkpoint, not with C. The codec is incomplete (no SILK, hybrid, Ogg Opus or other sample rates), and the README says it is not a production replacement for libopus. The timing corpus is licensed local audio that is not in the repo, and the raw timing JSONs are published only as SHA-256 hashes, so the run cannot be reproduced as published. The repository was archived on 2026-08-25 in favour of wavey-ai/soundkit (soundkit-opus). The README's soundkit-opus/libopus-rs link returned 404 on main. The crates.io release predates the measured optimisations.

notes: Real, honest first-party comparison against trunk libopus. It falls short of A because the baseline library's build flags were not recorded and the corpus is private, which matters at a 1-2% margin. The record wrongly said compiler versions were missing; the report states Rust 1.97.1 and GCC 12.2.0. Archived status is a caveat, not a reject. The successor wavey-ai/soundkit is public (MIT, 3 stars) and has a soundkit-opus directory; it was not verified.

tier_reason: reference/speed/README.md (Results, 2026-08-23) has every quoted number (e.g. SILK NB 8 kb/s 218x vs 195x, CELT 128 kb/s stereo 204x vs 116x = 1.76x, SILK NB decode 3432x vs 3958x). The harness is public: reference/speed/run.sh, reference/speed/cspeed.c, reference/rust/src/speed.rs, and reference/build.sh, which builds a sha256-pinned libopus 1.6.1 with CMake Release. Flags and the CPU (Apple M1 Pro) are stated. Neither compiler version is: rustc appears only as the 1.88.0 MSRV, and the C side is the system cc (clang per the README text), unversioned. corrections.workload: Encode and decode of generated, bit-reproducible 48 kHz test signals (speech for the SILK/hybrid rows with application voip and signal voice; music for the CELT rows with application audio, fullband, signal music), 20 ms frames, complexity 9 (plus complexity 0/5/10 rows), 8 s of audio per case. Fastest of 12 passes, a fresh encoder per pass built outside the timed region, OPUS_SET_LSB_DEPTH(24), and libopus constrained VBR at its default. Covers SILK, hybrid and CELT modes, mono and stereo.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 2 stars, 3 forks, 19 commits; crates.io opus-pure 0.2.2 (2026-09-28), 15,474 downloads
corrections.caveats: One aarch64 machine (Apple M1 Pro) only, no x86 numbers, and the toolchain versions are not pinned. Decode is slower than libopus in 9 of 10 rows (0.84-0.92x), with parity at 1.02x only for stereo hybrid. The large wins are CELT encode only (1.34-1.76x). SILK encode is a fixed-point port, so the float-libopus column compares different algorithms. Against fixed-point libopus, SILK encode is 0.97-1.11x and hybrid encode 1.09-1.13x. The README says hybrid matches neither libopus build exactly. Encoder output is not bit-exact with libopus except SILK, which is byte-exact against fixed-point libopus in 22 configurations. CELT and hybrid encoders are only interoperable, with 433 of 440 whole-stream configurations decoding within 100 dB SNR of libopus. Delivered bitrate is checked per row, and CELT lands within 0-1% of target on both stacks. In SILK the crate is slightly slower than libopus at complexity 0 and 5 (0.97x, 0.95x). The code derives from rusty-opus 0.9.1, itself a fork of restsend/opus-rs (both BSD-3-Clause), per ATTRIBUTION.md.

notes: The comparison is careful and like-for-like in settings: matched bitrate, complexity, application, bandwidth and signal; a fresh encoder per pass; delivered-bitrate and mode-mismatch flags. It would be tier A if the rustc and Apple clang versions were recorded. The ancestor restsend/opus-rs is from the same organisation as rustrtc; check whether rusty-opus or opus-rs are already listed before enrichment.

tier_reason: The README benchmark (release 0.3.141) carries every quoted number, and it formally has the A fields: public harness (examples/benchmark.rs, examples/go_bench/benchmark.go), rustc 1.97.1 and go 1.24.4, Cargo.toml release profile (fat LTO, codegen-units=1), and an i7-9700T. But the harness does not run the same work on each stack. rustrtc's channel comes from DataChannelConfig's derived Default (ordered=false, so DCEP type 0x80 reliable-unordered). webrtc-rs 0.17.1 and pion v3.3.6 default to ordered reliable channels, and only the pion sender is gated by a 100 KB bufferedAmount threshold. A first-party, mismatched comparison is C.

corrections.baseline: webrtc-rs 0.17.1 (Rust) and pion/webrtc v3.3.6 (Go); no C or C++ stack (libwebrtc, libdatachannel, usrsctp) was compared
corrections.workload: WebRTC data-channel loopback benchmark (cargo run -r --example benchmark): 10 concurrent peer-connection pairs in one process (ICE/DTLS/SCTP, each with an idle Opus audio track), each sending 1 KiB messages on one data channel for 10 s. Throughput = bytes received / whole run time including setup (MiB/s, labelled MB/s). 'Setup latency' = time from connected to data-channel open, not ICE/DTLS setup; pion's is truncated to whole ms. CPU and RSS are sampled with ps every 500 ms. rustrtc's channel is reliable unordered (DataChannelConfig default ordered=false); webrtc-rs and pion channels are reliable ordered. The pion sender throttles on a 100 KB bufferedAmount threshold, while the Rust senders yield every 32 sends.
corrections.claimed_speedup: README, release 0.3.141: throughput 549.04 MB/s vs 165.98 (webrtc-rs) and 169.58 (pion), about 3.3x and 3.2x; message rate 562,214 vs 169,967 and 173,648 msg/s; data-channel open latency 0.45 ms vs 25.64 and 3.00 ms; peak RSS 21 MB vs 44 and 48 MB; CPU 739.62% vs 677.95% and 555.20% (higher for rustrtc); throughput per CPU-percent 0.74 vs 0.24 and 0.31 MB/s.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: rustc 1.97.1 (8bab26f4f 2026-07-14) with Cargo.toml [profile.release] lto="fat", codegen-units=1, strip=symbols. This applies to both rustrtc and webrtc-rs, which are built into the same example binary by cargo run -r --example benchmark. go 1.24.4 linux/amd64, default go build for the pion program.
corrections.hardware: Intel Core i7-9700T @ 2.00GHz (8 cores), Debian 13, kernel 6.12.101+deb13-amd64
corrections.stars_or_usage: 110 stars, 20 forks, 352 commits; crates.io rustrtc 0.3.145 (2026-10-03), 15,220 downloads
corrections.caveats: This is networking, not audio or video coding. The benchmark measures WebRTC data channels (SCTP over DTLS over UDP loopback), with no RTP media, codec or SRTP work in the timed path. The baselines are a Rust stack (webrtc-rs) and a Go stack (pion v3.3.6, an old major version), not C or C++; libwebrtc, libdatachannel and usrsctp were not compared. The configurations differ. rustrtc's channel is reliable unordered (DataChannelConfig derives Default, so ordered=false), while webrtc-rs and pion default to ordered reliable channels. Only pion's sender waits on a 100 KB bufferedAmount threshold. Pion's latency is integer milliseconds. The 'setup latency' figure is data-channel open time after connection, not full connection setup. These are the author's own numbers from one run on one 2019 low-power desktop CPU (i7-9700T), taken at release 0.3.141 while HEAD is 0.3.145. Throughput is MiB/s labelled MB/s, and rustrtc uses more CPU in absolute terms.

notes: No C baseline at all: the comparison is against webrtc-rs and pion only. WebRTC data channels are networking, not audio/video coding, so the category should move to a networking/transport category (orchestrator's call). The headline 3.3x compares rustrtc's unordered channel with ordered channels in both baselines (verified in src/transports/datachannel.rs at HEAD, webrtc-rs v0.17.1 peer_connection/mod.rs and pion v3.3.6 peerconnection.go), so the comparison is not like-for-like.
